title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Control flow means which step runs next. In one sentence each: in a workflow, what decides it, and in an agent, what decides it?

A program handles each student message in three steps: (1) one model call pulls the machine and date out of the message, (2) the program calls the check_calendar tool with those values, (3) one model call writes the reply from the result. Which description fits best?

options.text: An agent, because it uses a tool the model cannot run itself
An agent, because the model is called more than once per request
A workflow, because the code fixes the order of the steps
An agent, because it reads and writes natural language

items.stem: Your team wants one part of the makerspace assistant built as a fixed workflow rather than an agent. Which part is the best choice?

options.text: Helping a student plan a project that may need several machines, depending on what the earlier lookups turn up
Working out why a student's laser cut keeps coming out charred, from their settings, photos and the manuals
Answering open questions that might touch any of the machine manuals, with a different search each time
Booking a slot: check the machine is free, check the training, reserve it, then send a confirmation

items.stem: Your sponsor's model budget is small. For a task whose steps are the same every time, why does a fixed workflow suit that budget better than an agent?

options.text: The code sets how many model calls a request makes, so its cost is known up front
A workflow calls the model exactly once per request, so it is always the cheapest
Each model call costs less when a workflow makes it than when an agent does
Both cost about the same per request, so a workflow only saves development time

items.stem: A program asks the model to label each student message as 'manual question', 'booking' or 'other'. The program then runs a separate sequence of steps for each label. Who owns the control flow, and what is the system?

options.text: The model, because its label decides which sequence runs; it is an agent
The code, because the model only picks among sequences set up beforehand; it is a workflow
The model, because there are several sequences instead of one; it is an agent
Neither, because a labeling step makes it a third kind of system; it is a router

items.stem: Your manual-question workflow does two steps: search the manuals once, then write the answer. A student asks about the laser cutter, but the single search returns the 3D printer manual. What happens next in the workflow?

options.text: It repeats the search until the results match the laser cutter
It asks the model to choose a better step before going on
It goes on to the second step and writes an answer from that result
It turns itself into an agent for that one request
